title: EditorCommand

AddAssets.description:
Add imported assets with the provenance their import filled in
(11.39). The only way a non-font asset enters a scene.

AddFonts.description:
Add prepared fonts and the font assets their faces need (11.13).
The only way a font enters a scene.

AddGuide.description: Put a guide on the canvas (11.44): a line along `axis` at `position` pixels. The lowest free id is given to it.

ApplyPreset.description: Instantiate one phase of a starter motion preset at `atFrame`.

durationMs.description:
The preset's declared `duration` parameter, in milliseconds.
Absent applies the phase at its own length.

ApplyTextAnimatorPreset.description:
Put one of EffectCraft's text-animator presets (listing id
`ec.textanimator.<name>`) on a text: its animator replaces the
text's, and its keys start at `at_frame` (11.61). One undo entry;
a preset the engine cannot draw yet refuses by name.

Arithmetic.description:
Arithmetic: combines each colour channel with a value of your choice, on the colour as it was
before its alpha. Alpha is left alone.

clip.description: Keep every result between 0 and 1. Off, results may go above 1 but never below 0.

ArithmeticOperator.description:
What Arithmetic does to each colour channel with the value set for that channel.

And, Or and Xor work on the 8-bit values of the channel and the setting (0 to 255), as After
Effects does; the rest work on the values themselves, so a pixel above 1 stays above 1.

oneOf.description: A channel above the value goes to 0; one at or below it stays.
A channel below the value goes to 0; one at or above it stays.
1 where the channel reaches the value, 0 where it does not.

AssetApproval.description: A named person's approval of an asset for use.

at.description:
When they approved, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. Authoring metadata
only: nothing on the render path reads it (invariant 8).

user.description: The approving user, as the authorization layer names them (2.9).

AssetAvailability.description: Whether an asset's bytes are available where they are needed.

AssetKind.description:
The kind of thing an asset is. `Font` is here so the asset store and the
font subsystem agree on what a font asset is.

AssetLibraryItem.description:
An asset as the library knows it. Carries **both** addresses: the content
hash (immutable, addresses the store) and the project-relative path
(mutable, addresses the library). The hash is what a scene's bindings
resolve against, so re-importing over the same path — a new render of the
same logo — updates the hash but never the binding.

assetId.description: Stable scene-facing id. Survives relink; distinct from any storage id.

checksum.description: Content hash — the store address. `None` only while importing.

colorSpace.description:
The colour space an image's pixel values are in (3.17, user decision
15 Nov 2026). Set at import from the file's own tag when it has one,
otherwise by the user; never inferred (B.1). An image without one is
refused by name when drawn.

name.description: Display name, separate from the on-disk name (ADR-0002 B.3).

provenance.description:
Where the bytes came from and under what terms (11.39). Every record
carries one, and it is always written: a human-made asset may leave
every field empty, but the schema is present in every saved project.

AssetOrigin.description: Who or what produced an asset's content.

oneOf.description: A person made it, including a file a person brought into the project.

A deterministic tool derived it from other inputs: a conversion, an
export or a render.
A generative model produced it.

AssetProvenance.description: Where an asset's bytes came from and under what terms.

c2paManifest.description: An attached C2PA manifest: a project-relative path or a URI.

promptHash.description:
SHA-256 of the prompt a model was given. The prompt text is not
stored with the asset.

provider.description:
Who supplied the bytes: a font service, a stock library, a model
vendor.

sources.description:
What the asset was made or fetched from: file names, URLs, the content
hashes of input assets. Always written, so the field is visible in a
saved project even when it is empty.

BezierPath.description:
A cubic bezier path, structured like Lottie/Bodymovin's "sh" shape so it
round-trips with the web's proven vector-animation format. Segment k→k+1 is
a cubic bezier; tangents are relative to their vertex. All three arrays
must be the same length — the constraint that also makes a path animatable.

autoTension.description:
Tension of the `auto` handles, 0 to 1 (default 0.5: centripetal
Catmull-Rom). Absent means the default.

vertexIds.description:
A stable id per vertex (11.112), parallel to `vertices`; absent on old
scenes (the vertex index then stands for it). Ids survive inserts,
deletes, reversal and undo, so two keys of an animated path correspond
by id, never by index.

vertexKinds.description:
The kind of each vertex (11.113), parallel to `vertices`; absent means
"inferred from the handles" as before. An `auto` vertex's stored handles
are ignored: [`BezierPath::effective`] derives them.

BlackWhite.description:
Black & White: a greyscale whose brightness per hue is set by six weights (red, yellow,
green, cyan, blue, magenta, interpolated round the wheel), optionally tinted.

reds.description: -2-3 each; 0.5 leaves the luminance alone, more brightens that hue, less darkens it.

tint.description: Colour the greyscale with the hue and saturation of `tint_color`.

BlendMode.description:
Every blend mode the authoring vocabulary contains, supported or not.

The first ten are 1.x's `MATERIAL_BLEND_MODES`, unchanged in name and
order, because a scene authored there must mean the same thing here. 3.20
appends the rest of the Photoshop and After Effects Layer > Blending Mode
menus, so every mode a PSD, an After Effects project or a Figma file names
has exactly one variant and never a nearest neighbour. Together they are
the 27 Photoshop modes and the After Effects ones; the formulas are
EffectCraft's (`crates/color/src/blend.rs` at 9a7d3e7, MIT OR Apache-2.0),
ported with attribution in the render worker.

Two pairs share a formula and stay separate because the source menus name
them separately: `add` (After Effects) and `linear-dodge` (Photoshop's
"Linear Dodge (Add)"); `difference` and `classic-difference` differ only in
how layer opacity applies. `alpha-mask` and `inverse-alpha-mask` are After
Effects' Stencil Alpha and Silhouette Alpha under their 1.x names.

oneOf.description: After Effects Add: `b + s`, over-range kept.

The recorded live fault: 1.x's browser renderer had no `overlay`, so
it drew `screen` instead and nobody was told. It is in the vocabulary
because authors use it; it is not fixed-function, so an engine without
a shader compositing path must refuse it (invariant 18).

After Effects Stencil Alpha: the backdrop is kept where this layer is
opaque, everywhere on the stage.

After Effects Silhouette Alpha: the backdrop is cut out where this
layer is opaque, everywhere on the stage.

Photoshop and After Effects Dissolve: each pixel shows the layer or
the backdrop by a fixed per-pixel threshold against the layer's alpha.
After Effects Dancing Dissolve: Dissolve with a new pattern each frame.

After Effects Classic Color Burn: opacity fades the layer toward white
before the formula applies; negative results are kept.

After Effects Classic Color Dodge: opacity fades the layer toward
black before the formula applies.
Photoshop Linear Dodge (Add): the same formula as `add`.

After Effects Classic Difference: opacity fades the layer toward black
before the formula applies.

After Effects Stencil Luma: the backdrop is scaled by this layer's
luminance, everywhere on the stage.

After Effects Silhouette Luma: the backdrop is scaled by one minus
this layer's luminance, everywhere on the stage.
After Effects Alpha Add: source-over colour, alpha `min(sa + da, 1)`.

After Effects Luminescent Premul: source-over colour without the
layer's own alpha clipping its over-range values.

BlurDimensions.description: Which axes a blur or glow spreads along.

useLegacy.description:
After Effects' legacy linear formula, which clips; otherwise tone
curves that keep black and white fixed.

BroadcastAction.description: What Broadcast Colors does to a colour whose signal is too high.

oneOf.description: Scale the whole colour down.
Pull the colour towards grey until it fits.
Make the unsafe pixels transparent.
Make the safe pixels transparent.

BroadcastColors.description:
Broadcast Colors: finds colours whose luma plus chroma goes over the maximum signal
amplitude of the chosen standard, and reduces or keys them.

BroadcastLocale.description: The broadcast standard Broadcast Colors measures against.

oneOf.description: NTSC: 7.5 IRE setup, chroma as I and Q.
PAL: no setup, chroma as U and V.

CcColorNeutralizer.description:
CC Color Neutralizer: moves the shadows, midtones and highlights each by the difference between
a balance colour and an unbalance colour (the cast to take out and the colour it should be).

blendWithOriginal.description: 0-1: how much of the original comes back.

pinning.description: 0-1: keeps pure black and pure white where they are.

CcColorOffset.description:
CC Color Offset: adds a phase to each channel (a full turn is the whole range), so a colour
cycles through the range.

redPhase.description: Degrees: 360 is a whole turn of the range.

CcThreshold.description: CC Threshold: black and white by whether the chosen channel reaches the level.

blend.description: 0-1: how much of the original comes back.

threshold.description: 0-255, as the level is set on an 8-bit picture.

CcThresholdRgb.description: CC Threshold RGB: each of red, green and blue made 0 or 1 at its own level.

blend.description: 0-1: how much of the original comes back.

CcToner.description:
CC Toner: maps the luminance of each pixel onto two, three or five colours, `blend` of the way
back to the original.

blend.description: 0-1: how much of the original comes back.

ChangeColor.description:
Change Color: shifts the hue, lightness and saturation of the pixels that match one colour,
softly at the edge of the match.

lightnessTransform.description: -1-1: a share of the way to white (or to black).

matchingSoftness.description: 0-1: the fade from a full match to none, past the tolerance.

matchingTolerance.description: 0-1: how far from the colour a pixel may be and still match fully.

saturationTransform.description: -1-1: a share of the way to full (or no) saturation.

oneOf.description: The picture with the change applied.
The matte of what matches, white on black.

ChangeMatch.description: How Change Color decides a pixel is the colour to change.

oneOf.description: Distance in RGB.
Distance in hue only (greys match no hue).
Distance in chromaticity, whatever the brightness.

ChannelMixer.description:
Channel Mixer: each output channel is a weighted sum of the input channels. With
`monochrome` the red row drives all three.

ChannelSource.description: Where Shift Channels takes a channel's value from.

CloseScene.description: Close a session; a dirty session refuses unless `force`.

ColorBalance.description: Color Balance: shifts the shadows, midtones and highlights (by luminance) toward a colour.

preserveLuminosity.description: Keep each pixel's luminance and change only its colour.

ColorBalanceHls.description:
Color Balance (HLS): shifts hue, lightness and saturation of every pixel. Lightness and
saturation move a share of the way to the extreme (or to zero); hue wraps.

ColorDiffView.description:
Which stage of Color Difference Key Color Difference Key shows. (EffectCraft also has a
four-up view; it needs each pixel's position, so it comes with the coordinate pass.)

oneOf.description: The picture as it came in.
The picture with the key applied.

matteBlack.description: The matte's own levels (its output stays 0 to 255): input black and white, and gamma.

ColorOverflow.description: What CC Color Offset does with a channel pushed past white.

oneOf.description: Start again from black.
Fold back down from white.
Snap to black or white.

ColorRange.description:
Color Range: keys out every pixel inside a box in a colour space, fading over the fuzziness
past the box. All bounds are on the 0 to 255 scale of the space chosen, whose three axes are
named L, a, b for Lab; Y, U, V for YUV; and R, G, B for RGB.

fuzziness.description: 0-255: the fade past the box, in the same units. 0 is a hard edge.

minA.description: On the second axis (a, U or G).

minB.description: On the third axis (b, V or B).

minL.description: The box's lower and upper bound on the first axis (L, Y or R).

ColorShift.description: A colour shift for one tonal range, -1-1 per channel.

ColorValue.description:
An authored paint: nothing, a colour, or a gradient.

`None` is a value, not an absence — "the author turned the fill off" and
"the author has not set a fill" are different states, and collapsing them
is how a transparent object becomes a black one on the other renderer.
Ported from 1.x `ColorValue`, with every colour now tagged.

angle.description: Degrees, clockwise from the positive X axis.

ConfirmDesignSystem.description: Confirm a design-system draft as the project's next version.

ContentHash.description: Content address of asset bytes: SHA-256, lowercase hex.

ControlField.description: One named property an operator is allowed to fill on a template.

ControlFieldKind.description: The kind of value an operator may enter for a declared field.

ControlValue.description: A typed value supplied to a declared control field.

CreateProject.description: Create an empty project in the store.

CreateShape.description:
Create a shape from a bezier path (3.13). The path's own coordinates
place it; its fill is grey and its stroke off until `setPaint` and
`setStroke` say otherwise.

compoundPaths.description:
Additional subpaths, drawn with the primary path as one
compound shape under its fill rule; absent or empty is one path.

CubicBezier.description:
Cubic-bezier control points for a custom outgoing easing.

`x1` and `x2` stay in 0–1 because they are time controls; y may overshoot
provided the resulting segment stays within the property's range (opacity
0–1, width/height non-negative). Other properties permit overshoot.
The points are stored with the
key, not solved from neighbouring keys at display time, so a saved scene
means the same curve when it is reopened.

CurvePoint.description: A control point of a tone curve, both coordinates 0–1.

Curves.description:
Curves: each channel is a monotone cubic through its points (at least
two), extended linearly beyond the end points. Colour channels go through
the RGB curve first, then their own.

DeleteScene.description:
Delete a stored scene. With `if_revision` the scene is deleted only
if it is still the revision the caller read (8.12); the MCP surface
requires it, so an agent never deletes work it has not seen.

DesignSystemCommit.description:
A draft plus the human confirming it (G.2, build plan 10.4).

The confirmation is deliberately *not* a field on [`DesignSystemDraft`]. A
draft is a proposal, and a proposal that can carry its own confirmation is
one an importer could fill in on the reviewer's behalf — which is exactly
the auto-accept G.2 forbids. Keeping it in the request makes confirming an
act a caller performs rather than a property the draft already had.

confirmedBy.description: Who accepted it. Recorded into provenance; never invented.

DesignSystemDraft.description: A lossless import proposal. It cannot become active without confirmation.

DesignSystemSource.description:
The complete source document retained beside an imported draft.

Import is deliberately not a destructive projection. The mapped tokens are
what GrapiX can enforce; `document` is the source **as supplied**, so a
reviewer can inspect and re-export everything it actually contained.

It is the original text rather than a re-print of the parse, and `sha256`
is taken over those same bytes. A hash over a re-serialisation answers "is
this equivalent to what we parsed?", which is not the question provenance
asks: a duplicated JSON key, or a number re-spelled by whichever toolchain
last wrote the file, would silently change what the record refers to.

DesignSystemSourceKind.description: The external format a design-system draft came from.

DraftVisualTokens.description:
Visual tokens while an import is awaiting human review.

`min_text_size` stays optional here and required in [`VisualTokens`]. An
importer may not invent a legibility threshold merely to make a draft look
complete; confirmation refuses until a human supplies one.

DuplicateScene.description: Copy a stored scene under a new id and name.

EditPath.description:
One semantic operation on one path (11.107, the Pen spec's path
commands): insert, delete or convert vertices, set a handle, move
vertices, reshape a segment, reverse, restart or close. `target`
names a shape's subpath or a mask; the result is checked as
`setShapePath` or `setObjectMasks` checks it.

baseRevision.description:
For a path that is linked (11.112): the revision the edit was made on. The edit is refused when the
shared path has been edited since.

frame.description:
The frame an edit of an animated path is made at (11.112): a
move, handle or kind edit sets the key there; an edit of which
vertices there are (insert, delete, reverse, first vertex,
close) lands in every key at once. Left out, the path is static.

EditProperty.description: A property value edit; with `autoKey` it also upserts a key at `frame`.

EditScene.description:
Apply an ordered, atomic edit batch to one document. One batch is
one undo entry, tagged with the module that issued it.

Against a stored scene the batch is a compare-and-swap (8.12):
`if_revision` is the revision the caller read, the write lands only
if that is still the stored scene's revision, and the outcome
carries the new one. The MCP surface requires it for a stored
target; a session target has no stored revision and must not name
one.

EditorModule.description:
The Editor module a gesture came from (11.37). Undo scoped to a module
reverses only batches tagged with it; an untagged batch belongs to
`Scene`. The surface that issues a gesture names its own module, because
guessing it from edit kinds would misfile a gesture that touches several.

EffectInstance.description: One entry in an object's effect stack.

effectId.description:
Stable within the object: keyframe channels address the effect by it,
so reordering the stack keeps every channel valid.

enabled.description: A disabled effect is skipped entirely. Keyframable with hold keys.

maskIds.description:
Mask Reference (3.28): the ids of masks of the same object that limit
this effect. The effect shows only where they cover, the rest of the
layer keeps what it was before this effect. Absent or empty: the whole
layer. A referenced mask counts even in mode `none`.

EffectPoint.description: A point in the layer's own pixels.

EmbeddingPolicy.description:
Whether a font's bytes may travel inside a `.gpxpkg` — the licensing
decision made per font (docs/p2-licensing-positions.md §5).

oneOf.description: Bytes may be packaged (licence permits redistribution: OFL, Apache…).
Package carries the reference; the render node resolves and caches.
Workstation-only; bytes never leave the operator's machine.

Exposure.description: Exposure, in linear light whatever the working space.

Extract.description:
Extract: keeps the pixels whose chosen channel lies between the black and white points (0 to
255) and fades the rest over the softness.

blackSoftness.description: 0-255: the fade below the black point.

whiteSoftness.description: 0-255: the fade above the white point.

FeatherPoint.description:
A point of a mask's variable feather (11.108, Masking spec v2 4.6): where on the mask's path it sits (segment `segment`, parameter `t`),
how far the edge softens there and how smoothly that blends into the next point.

radius.description:
Signed, in pixels of the layer: positive softens the edge outward, negative inward; the transition spans `|radius|` on that
side only. Zero is a hard edge there.

segment.description: The segment of the mask's path the point is on.

tension.description: 0 to 1: how the radius changes toward the next point: 0 in a straight line, 1 smoothly (smoothstep).

FigmaColor.description: A colour as Figma's plugin API reports it: `0..1` per channel, sRGB.

FigmaNode.description: One node of the frame, in Figma's own vocabulary.

cornerRadii.description: Top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, when the corners differ.

cornerRadius.description: One radius for all four corners.

id.description: Figma's node id, such as `3300:2528`. It is the scene object's id, so a re-import lines up.

rotation.description: Figma's rotation in degrees (counter-clockwise positive), about the node's top-left.

x.description: Relative to the root frame's top-left.

FigmaPaint.description: One paint of a fill or a stroke.

opacity.description: The paint's own opacity, on top of the colour's alpha.

oneOf.description:
A linear gradient across the node's box at `angle` degrees, clockwise from the
positive X axis (0 runs left to right, 90 top to bottom).
A radial gradient centred in the node's box, reaching its edges.

A picture fill. `image` names a PNG or WebP in the project's `Images/<frame>/` folder
(the file name without its extension, as exported from Figma); the ingest finds it
there and draws it. A picture that is not there is named on the report with the path
to file it at.

image.description: Figma's `imageHash`, or the file name the agent exported the picture to.

FigmaText.description: A text node's content and style.

lineHeightPx.description: Line height in pixels; absent means the font's own.

Fill.description: Paints the layer's pixels with a colour, keeping their coverage.

opacity.description: 0–1: how much of the colour replaces the layer's own.

FontDefinition.description:
A family as the scene knows it: its faces, fallbacks and licensing
posture. Embedded verbatim in the scene document, so a package is
self-describing.

license.description:
The declared licence. A `Package` font without one is a preflight
refusal (p2-licensing-positions §5: unstated licence ⇒ restricted).

FontFaceDefinition.description: One face of a family: weight/style/stretch with a source.

FontFormat.description:
Font container formats the pipeline accepts. WOFF/WOFF2 are delivery
wrappers; the shaper sees the same tables either way.

FontLoadStatus.description:
Load state of a font or face. `Missing` at preflight is a refusal
(`Refusal::FontMissing`), never a fallback to a system font.

oneOf.description: Linked source declared but not yet resolved; cannot preflight.

FontSource.description:
Where a face's bytes come from.

`rename_all_fields` (not `rename_all`) because the variant *fields* are
what hit the wire: `rename_all` alone would leave `asset_id` snake_case
while every other contract is camelCase.

oneOf.description: Packaged asset bytes, content-addressed.

originalUrl.description: Original public URL when this face was resolved and cached from CSS.

stylesheetUrl.description: Stylesheet that declared this cached face.

oneOf.description: A CSS stylesheet declaring `@font-face` rules (Google Fonts class).
An Adobe Fonts project. Reference-only by licence; never packaged.
A direct HTTPS font file URL.

GammaChannel.description: One channel of Gamma/Pedestal/Gain: `pedestal + (gain - pedestal) * v^gamma`.

GammaPedestalGain.description: Gamma/Pedestal/Gain, per colour channel, with a Black Stretch that lifts low values.

blackStretch.description: 0-10: lifts the dark end of every channel; 0 is off.

GoToHistoryStep.description:
Take a session to the state just after one step of its change history (11.82),
or to before every listed step when `step` is left out. It is what the right
number of undos or redos gives, done in one replay: every step up to and
including the named one is applied (one a module-scoped undo had skipped too),
and every later step is undone and can be redone in its order. The jump is not
itself a step, and going to where the session already is changes nothing. A
replay that refuses changes nothing (`historyConflict`); a step the history no
longer lists refuses `historyStepUnknown`.

step.description: The step's `id` from [`HistoryView`]; left out for the scene as opened.

GradientCoordinateMode.description:
Whether a gradient's coordinates are the object's or the scene's. An
object-space gradient follows its object; a scene-space one stays put
while the object moves through it.

GradientSpread.description: What a gradient does outside its 0–1 span. CSS's own names.

oneOf.description: A vertical line at an x position.
A horizontal line at a y position.

HandleCoupling.description: How the far handle follows (see [`Coupling`]), on the wire.

ImportAsset.description:
File one file into a project (11.43), from a file on this machine: a picture
(png, webp, jpg, jpeg, svg) into `Assets/Images`, a video (mp4, mov, avi, webm) into
`Assets/Videos`, audio (wav, mp3) into `Assets/Audio`, a 3D model (gltf, glb, obj, fbx,
stl, ply, dae, usd, usdz) into `Assets/Models`, or a font (otf, ttf, woff, woff2)
into `Fonts`. The bytes decide which, not the name. The same bytes filed again are a
no-op, and different bytes under an existing name refuse. The outcome's imported
effect names the filed path and its content hash.

folder.description:
One folder name under the class folder (a Figma frame's name, say); empty for
the class folder itself.

from.description: An absolute path to the file on this machine.

name.description: The file name to file it under; the source file's name when absent.

source.description: What the file came from (a Figma node, a URL), kept in its record.

ImportFigma.description:
Ingest one Figma frame into a new stored scene (18.2, 18.3). The user's own agent
reads the frame through Figma's MCP and passes the text of `get_metadata` as
`metadata`; GrapiX holds no Figma token and makes no network call. The frame becomes
the canvas (its width and height), its nodes become objects at their Figma positions,
and the report names everything `get_metadata` does not carry (fills, text content,
fonts, radii, clipping). The metadata text is retained in the project by content
hash. Refuses an existing id; one frame per call.

frame.description:
The full-fidelity route: the frame as the agent read it through Figma's MCP
(fills, strokes, radii, text, fonts, blend modes), in the typed shape of
[`FigmaNode`]. Exactly one of `frame` and `metadata` is given.

imageFolder.description:
The folder under `Images` the frame's pictures are filed in; the root frame's
name when absent. A picture fill's `image` is looked up there as `<image>.png`,
then `<image>.webp`.

metadata.description:
The structure-only route: the reply of Figma's `get_metadata` for the frame,
as received. Positions and nesting only, with no paint and no text.

name.description: The scene's display name; the Figma frame's name when absent.

sourceName.description: What to call the retained source, for example the frame's name.

ImportScene.description:
Import an SVG into a new stored scene through the four-tier
pipeline (7.2). The source is adopted into the project by content
hash; the report is an `Imported` effect. Refuses an existing id.

name.description: The scene's display name; the source file's stem when absent.

sourceName.description: The source's own file name, kept in the report and the asset.

InkShift.description:
One colour range's adjustment in print inks, -1 to 1 each (-100% to 100%). Positive adds the
ink, negative removes it. `black` moves all three colour channels together.

Invert.description: Invert: `1 - v` on the chosen channels, blended back toward the original.

blendWithOriginal.description: 0–1: how much of the original comes back; 0 is a full inversion.

KeyMatch.description: How Linear Color Key measures how far a pixel is from the key colour.

KeyOperation.description: Which side of the key Linear Color Key makes transparent.

oneOf.description: The colours that match go transparent.
Only the colours that match stay.

KeyRef.description: One authored key a capture names: a property and the frame it sits on.

oneOf.description: The picture with the key applied.
The picture as it came in.
The matte: white where the picture is kept, on opaque black.

LeaveColor.description:
Leave Color: greys everything but one colour. `tolerance` is how far a pixel may be from it and
keep its colour; `edge_softness` fades the rest in over that much more.

amount.description: 0-1: how much of the greying is applied; 0 leaves the picture alone.

LeaveMatch.description: How Leave Color decides a pixel is the colour to keep.

oneOf.description: Distance in RGB.
Distance in hue only (greys match no hue).

Levels.description:
Levels: the RGB controls map every colour channel, then each channel's
own; the alpha controls map coverage where the layer drew.

clipToOutputBlack.description: Clip values below input black / above input white.

LicenseClass.description:
The terms an asset may be used under, as a class a show profile can test
(13.8) rather than free licence text.

oneOf.description: Made by or for the production, which holds the rights.
Third-party, licensed for commercial broadcast.

An open licence that permits commercial use: OFL, CC0, CC BY,
Apache-2.0, MIT.
GPL-class: obligations attach when it is redistributed.
Licensed for non-commercial use only, such as CC BY-NC.
Licensed for editorial or news use only.
Limited by territory, term or medium.

LimiterCompression.description: How far below the clip level the soft knee starts.

LimiterLevel.description: The level Video Limiter clips to, as a share of white.

LimiterMethod.description: What Video Limiter limits: brightness, colour, or both.

oneOf.description: Compress the luminance, keep each channel's offset from it.
Pull the colour towards its luminance until every channel fits.
Both, luminance first.

LinearColorKey.description:
Linear Color Key: makes the pixels near one colour transparent (or keeps only them), fading
over the softness past the tolerance.

tolerance.description: 0-1: how far from the key a pixel may be and still be keyed out fully.

LinkPaths.description:
Make `target`'s path the same path as `source`'s (11.112): the numbers of `source` are copied in and the
two are one linked path from then on, an edit of either changing both. A mask is given an id when it has
none. Refused when either path is animated or `target` is linked already.

Mask.description: One layer mask (3.19): a closed path in the object's own coordinates.

expansion.description:
Grows (positive) or shrinks (negative) the mask outward from its
path, in pixels.

falloff.description: How the feather falls off (3.27); a Gaussian when absent.

feather.description:
Softens the edge: a Gaussian blur of the mask's coverage, in pixels
(the blur's standard deviation is half of it).

featherPoints.description:
Variable feather (11.108): when there are points, the edge softens by the amount the points give along the path (blended around
the closed contour by distance along it) instead of by `feather`, which then does nothing. Absent or empty: the uniform feather.

featherY.description:
The feather across the other axis, in pixels; absent, the same as
`feather` (3.27). Both are in the object's own pixels, so the viewer's
zoom never changes them.

id.description:
A name that stays with the mask when the stack is reordered or renamed,
which an effect's mask reference points at (3.28). Absent for a mask
nothing refers to; unique within the object when present.

MaskFalloff.description: How a mask's feather falls off across its edge (3.27, Masking spec v2).

oneOf.description: A Gaussian: the edge ramps like an S, softest at the ends.
A box of the feather's width: the edge ramps in a straight line.

MaskMode.description: How a mask combines with the masks above it (3.19), After Effects' modes.

oneOf.description: Ignored: the mask is kept but shapes nothing.
Union with the masks above.
Removes its area from the masks above.
Keeps only where it overlaps the masks above.

Keeps where exactly one of it and the masks above covers; on soft
coverage the absolute difference of the two (the Masking spec v2's
baseline, `|a - c|`).
Keeps the larger of its coverage and the masks above's.
Keeps the smaller of its coverage and the masks above's.

MatchAccuracy.description: How exactly Color Difference Key measures colour: on the values as they are, or on light.

MatteLevels.description:
A levels control on a matte: input black and white and output black and white on a 0 to 255
scale, and a gamma.

MixerRow.description: One output channel's mix: how much of each input channel it takes, plus a constant.

MotionTokens.description:
Motion tokens: the primitives every preset composes from (G.6.1).

Durations and staggers are milliseconds. Easings are cubic-bezier control
points, or the literal `hold` for a phase that must not interpolate.

stagger.description: Named stagger intervals in ms, e.g. `tight: 40`, `base: 70`.

MoveGuide.description: Move a guide to another position.

MovePathKey.description:
Move a path key to another frame (11.112); a frame that has a key
already is refused, as `moveKeyframe` refuses it.

NamedEasing.description: An easing token: a cubic-bezier curve, or `hold`.

oneOf.description: A named cubic-bezier: `[x1, y1, x2, y2]`.
A named hold: no interpolation between keys.

ObjectField.description:
A typed inspector field/value pair. The adjacent tag makes an invalid field
and value combination unrepresentable on the command wire.

oneOf.description:
The object's box (`ObjectBase.width`, `height`): a rect and an image
fill it, an ellipse is inscribed in it, paragraph text wraps inside it.
Finite and not negative, as the engine draws it.
Draw order within a layer (`ObjectBase.z_index`).

The text choices of the Properties dock (11.132): held values that are never keyframed. Text objects only. Whether the engine
draws a value is not decided here: `text_choices` asks the drawability check, and a graphic that uses a value the engine
cannot draw yet is refused by name when it is previewed or published, exactly as when it is loaded.
Horizontal lines, or upright columns running right to left or left to right (11.51).
First-line indent in scene units (11.51): the first line of every paragraph starts this far in. Not negative.

Hide when empty (11.153, `ObjectBase.hide_when_empty`): the element is not drawn while one of its text or image bindings resolves to a
missing, null or blank value. Turning it on is refused by name on an element with no such binding; turning it off always works.

OpenScene.description: Open a document in a new session.

PaintSlot.description: Which of an object's two paints `SetPaint` sets.

PathAddress.description: A path in the scene, addressed from outside by its place in its object (`target`).

PathOp.description:
One semantic change to one path. Each is exact and refuses by name what
it cannot do; a whole gesture is one of these, so one undo step.

oneOf.description: A vertex on `segment` at `t`, the curve unchanged (De Casteljau).
Vertices taken out; the curves beside them join with their handles.
A corner made smooth, or a vertex with handles made a corner.
A vertex taken out with one curve fitted over the two beside it, kept only when the shape stays within `tolerance` (11.113).
One handle set to `vector` (an offset from its vertex).
Vertices moved by `delta`, their handles with them.
The curve dragged at `t` of `segment` by `delta`; its ends stay.
The same outline drawn the other way.
A closed path started from vertex `index`.
The path closed or opened.
A vertex given a kind: corner, smooth, symmetric or auto (11.113).
The tension of the path's `auto` vertices, 0 to 1 (11.113).

PathTarget.description: Which path of an object an `editPath` edit changes.

oneOf.description:
A shape's path: `subpath` 0 is its main path, 1 and on its compound
subpaths in order.
One of the object's masks, by its place in the list.

PhaseKind.description:
The operator phases a scene timeline can name.

These are exactly `crate::mcp::MOTION_PHASES`, and a test below pins them
against it: a phase added to one and not the other fails the gate rather
than producing a scene the agent surface cannot describe.

oneOf.description: Build on. Triggered by Take.
Idle loop after `in` completes. Interruptible at any frame.
Build off. Triggered by Out.
A staged build, triggered by Continue. A timeline may carry several.
How a bound value changes on air without a full re-take.

PhotoFilter.description:
Photo Filter: multiplies the picture by a filter colour, `density` of the way, optionally
keeping the pixel's luminance.

PhotoFilterPreset.description: The camera and colour filters Photo Filter offers. `Custom` uses the effect's own colour.

Posterize.description: Posterize: each colour channel snaps to `level` evenly spaced values.

ProvenanceTool.description: The tool, or for model origin the model, that made or imported the bytes.

RangeSpace.description: The colour space Color Range measures a pixel in. Lab is the default.

oneOf.description: CIE Lab, scaled so L runs 0 to 255 and a and b are centred on 128.
Y, U and V, with U and V centred on 128.
Red, green and blue, 0 to 255.

RationalRate.description:
A frame rate as an exact rational. Never a float (invariant 12).

29.97 is 30000/1001 and cannot be represented in binary floating point.
Accumulating a rounded rate across an 8-hour soak drifts the clock, so this
type deliberately offers no `f64` constructor.

Redo.description: Reapply the latest undone batch, or the latest one `module` issued.

RelinkAsset.description: Point a library asset at new bytes, keeping its id and bindings.

RelinkMaterial.description: Repoint every use of one material to another.

RemoveColorMatting.description:
Remove Color Matting: takes a background colour back out of a picture that was matted against
it, so its edges stop carrying a halo.

clipHdr.description: Keep every channel at or under the alpha.

RemoveFont.description:
Remove one font nothing names, with the font assets no other font
uses. The only way a font leaves a scene.

RemoveGuide.description: Take a guide off the canvas.

RemovePathKey.description:
Take one path key off a path channel (11.112). The last key's
removal ends the channel and leaves the path as that key had it.

RemoveSubpath.description:
Take one subpath out of a compound shape (11.112): the others keep their contour ids, and the path channels and links of
the shape follow them to their new places; those of the subpath taken out end with it. A shape keeps at least one path.

ReplaceControl.description: Replace the declared control with the same `fieldId`.

ReplaceFont.description:
Replace a font's faces and files under the same id (11.13): what
names the font keeps naming it, and its display name, fallbacks
and enabled state are kept.

Revision.description:
Publish revision. Exact-match only: a take against a stale revision is
refused, never coerced (invariant 17).

Rgba.description:
A colour, with the space it was authored in.

Components are 0–1 floats rather than 8-bit bytes because the working
space is linear and 8 bits of linear has visible banding in the shadows.

SaveMotionPreset.description:
Save the selected keys of one object as one phase of a motion
preset in the project's library (11.15). The document is read, never
written: saving a preset is not a scene edit and is not undoable.

oneOf.description: Update the stored scene the session is bound to; it must exist.
Create the scene in a project; it must not exist. Binds the session.
Write a scene file.

Save the session as the next numbered version of itself (11.30), and continue in it.

A scene stored in a project is written, with its unsaved edits, as a new stored scene under
the next free id (`strap` gives `strap_v002`, `strap_v003` gives `strap_v004`, and a number
already taken is passed over) with the name numbered the same way. The version it came from
is not written to: it stays exactly as it was last saved. The session then belongs to the
new scene and starts a fresh history, because the scene it edits has a new identity. A scene
saved to a file is written beside it as the next numbered file (`strap.json` gives
`strap_v002.json`), and the session continues in that file with its history. A scene that has
never been saved has no version to number from and refuses `sessionUnbound`. A failed write
changes nothing.

SceneEasing.description:
The easing between two keys. Closed and finite: the curve an author chooses
must be one every evaluator knows by name, because a substituted curve is a
visual change no one named (invariant 18).

oneOf.description:
Robert Penner's easeOutBounce: the value arrives at the second key and rebounds with shrinking height, ending exactly on
it. Never leaves the range between the two keys' values. Not a cubic bezier (11.134).

Robert Penner's easeOutElastic (amplitude 1, period 0.3): the value overshoots the second key and settles through a
decaying oscillation. It leaves the range between the keys' values by about 37 percent of their distance, so a property
with a range refuses it where that would break the range. Not a cubic bezier (11.134).

SceneEdit.description:
One change to one scene document. Only carried inside
`EditorCommand::EditScene` and only applied through [`apply_edits`].

SceneKeyframe.description: One key on one numeric property channel.

bezier.description: Custom bezier control points, present exactly when easing is custom.

easing.description: Outgoing easing toward the next key.

frame.description: Absolute frame at the scene canvas rate.

value.description: The property's value at that frame, in the property's own units.

oneOf.description: A fresh document built in Rust by `scene::new_scene`.
A scene file on disk.
A stored project scene; an already-open origin is reused.

An SVG document imported through the 7.2 pipeline. The text travels
whole so the hash in the report is the hash of what was supplied; the
session opens unbound, with the report as an `Imported` effect.

SceneTarget.description:
The document an edit batch applies to: an open session, or a scene in the
project store (read, edited and written back in one command).

SelectiveColor.description:
Selective Color: changes the amount of cyan, magenta, yellow and black ink in one range of
colours without touching the others. A pixel belongs to the primary and secondary range its
hue falls in, to whites by how light its darkest channel is, to blacks by how dark its
lightest channel is, and to neutrals by how close it sits to mid grey; the ranges' shifts are
summed by those weights.

SelectiveMethod.description:
How Selective Color reads its adjustments: a share of the ink a pixel already has
(Relative), or a flat amount (Absolute).

SessionKey.description:
Identity of one open editor session. A `u32`, so TS receives `number`
rather than `bigint` (memory rule 22). Keys are monotonic from 1.

SetAnchor.description:
Set the pivot every listed object rotates and scales about; left
out is the object's origin. Refuses a non-finite point by name.

SetAssetColorSpace.description:
Tag the colour space an image asset's pixel values are in (3.17):
what an untagged image needs before it can be drawn.

SetBinding.description: Bind `property` to a data path, or unbind it when `path` is absent.

SetBlendMode.description:
Set the layer blend mode of every listed object (3.20); left out
is `normal`. A kind that draws nothing itself (a group, a layer, a
marker, a camera, a light) refuses `objectFieldNotApplicable`.

SetCanvas.description:
Change the canvas: its rational frame rate and/or its size (11.43).
Frames are canonical (invariant 12): a rate change keeps every key
frame number and the duration in frames, so the graphic plays the
same frames at the new rate; only its wall-clock length changes.

SetClipChild.description:
Name a group's clip child, or clear it by leaving `clipChildId` out
(3.19). The clip child must be one of the group's own children and
draw pixels (`clipGroupInvalid`).

SetEffects.description:
Replace one object's ordered effect stack (3.22); empty clears it.
Each effect is checked as the validator checks it (`effectInvalid`).

SetGroupChildren.description:
Replace a group's ordered children (3.19). A child another group
already claims, a missing child and a cycle refuse
`sceneHierarchyInvalid`; a group is the only kind with children here.

SetObjectField.description: One inspector field over every listed object.

SetObjectMasks.description:
Replace one object's mask list; an empty list clears it (3.19).
Each mask refuses by name (`maskInvalid`, with its index) when the
engine cannot draw it as authored.

SetPaint.description:
Set one paint of every listed object to a colour or gradient, or
clear it by leaving `paint` out (3.17). A shape's fill or stroke
switch follows the paint.

SetPathKey.description:
Put a whole path key on a path channel (11.112), creating the
channel on its first key. A key at a frame that has one replaces it.

SetPreserveTransparency.description: Turn Preserve Underlying Transparency on or off for one layer (3.28).

SetSceneId.description: Change the id of a scene that is not bound to a stored origin.

SetSceneLabel.description: Change the Scene ID, the label a person edits (1.13). Nothing that points at the scene changes. An empty label takes it away.

SetShapePath.description:
Replace a shape's geometry: its path and every additional subpath
(a compound path); an empty list leaves one path. `fill_rule`, when
given, decides where overlapping subpaths fill (even-odd cuts a
hole); left out keeps the shape's rule.

SetStroke.description:
Set the stroke width and style of every listed object (3.17). A
style left out is the default: miter joins, butt caps, solid.

SetTextAnimator.description: Set a text animator, or remove it and its keys with null.

SetTrackMatte.description:
Set one object's track matte by its source's id, or clear it by
leaving `trackMatte` out (3.19). Refuses by name
(`trackMatteInvalid`) what cannot be drawn as authored.

SetTrim.description:
Set one shape's trim window (3.13): start and end in percent of the
path, offset in percent of a turn. A value left out is its default
(0, 100, 0); all three replace what the shape had.

ShiftChannels.description:
Shift Channels: each of alpha, red, green and blue takes its value from any channel of the
pixel (or a constant). The defaults take each from itself.

SourceColorSpace.description:
What a colour or a texture was authored in. There is no `Unknown`: an
untagged source is a defect the importer must refuse, not a value a
renderer may guess at (B.1, "never infer").

oneOf.description:
IEC 61966-2-1. What a hex literal, a PNG without an ICC profile and
most authoring tools mean.
Already linear — no decode on the way in.
ITU-R BT.709 with its own transfer curve. Broadcast source material.

SpillAccuracy.description: How exactly Spill Suppressor finds the spill.

oneOf.description: The key's strongest channel is held to the larger of the other two.
The part of each pixel that points along the key's colour is removed.

SpillSuppressor.description: Spill Suppressor: takes the cast of a keyed screen's colour out of the picture.

suppression.description: 0-2: how much of the spill goes.

StrokeCap.description: How a stroke ends an open path and each dash. SVG's and CSS's names.

StrokeJoin.description: How a stroke joins its segments. The names are SVG's and CSS's.

StrokeStyle.description:
A stroke's joins, caps and dash pattern (3.17). Lengths are in the
object's own units, like `strokeWidth`.

dash.description: Alternating dash and gap lengths; empty is a solid line.

dashOffset.description: How far into the dash pattern the stroke starts.

miterLimit.description: A miter join longer than this many stroke widths becomes a bevel.

StyleColor.description:
A text-style colour, either literal or resolved from the active project
design system when the style is applied.

StyleNumber.description:
A numeric text-style value, either literal or resolved from the active
project design system when the style is applied.

TakePage.description: A saved operator-filled instance of a template.

TextAnimator.description:
One geometry animator on a text object. Values describe the transform at
full selection; the range weights blend from the identity per cluster.

fill.description: Solid target colour for fully selected glyphs.

opacity.description: Fully selected paint opacity. Absent keeps the original paint alpha.

tracking.description: Signed spacing added after a fully selected shaped cluster, in scene pixels.

TextAutoFit.description: What to do when shaped text does not fit its box. Never silently clipped.

TextCase.description:
Case applied when the text is drawn, not when it is typed: the authored
characters stay as they are, so a data binding can replace the text and
the case still applies, and switching it off returns the author's own
capitalisation.

TextDecoration.description:
Underline and strikethrough: drawn from the font's metrics rather than
shaped, so they are object state and not part of the font definition.

TextLayout.description: Point text grows from its origin; paragraph text wraps inside the base box.

TextRangeBasis.description: The logical units a text range selects.

TextRangeSelector.description: Normalized range parameters. One unit of offset spans the entire text.

TextStyle.description:
A named, reusable subset of a text object's appearance.

Optional entries are deliberately absent rather than defaults: applying a
style must not overwrite a property its author did not declare.

Threshold.description: Threshold: pixels at or above `level` luminance become white, the rest black.

ThresholdChannel.description: What CC Threshold compares with the level.

oneOf.description: Each of red, green and blue on its own.
The coverage: the result is hard-edged.

TimelinePhase.description: One named span of the scene timeline.

endFrame.description: One past the last frame. See the module note on why this is exclusive.

name.description:
Distinguishes several `continue` phases from each other. Absent means
the kind names it uniquely, which is true of every kind but `continue`.

startFrame.description: First frame of the phase, inclusive.

Tint.description: Maps luminance to a colour ramp between two colours.

TokenMapping.description: One source value that became a GrapiX token.

TokenRef.description:
A token reference in a preset: `{duration.base}`, `{easing.brand-in}`.

A preset that hardcodes a value instead of referencing a token is a bug for
the same reason a component hardcoding a hex colour is (G.6.1). Kept as a
string with a checked shape rather than a free string, so a malformed
reference is caught at parse, not at render.

TonerTones.description: How many colours CC Toner maps the tones of the picture to.

oneOf.description: Shadows and highlights.
Shadows, midtones and highlights.
Shadows, darktones, midtones, brights and highlights.

TrackMatte.description: A layer's track matte (3.19): its source by explicit id, and the mode.

TrackMatteMode.description:
What a track matte takes from its source (3.19), After Effects' modes.
Luma is the Rec.709 weighting of the source's premultiplied working-space
colour, so a transparent source counts as black; values clamp to 0..1.

oneOf.description: The layer shows where the source is opaque.
The layer shows where the source is transparent.
The layer shows where the source is bright.
The layer shows where the source is dark.

Tritone.description:
Tritone: luminance maps to a ramp shadows, midtones, highlights; `blend_with_original`
brings the original colour back. The colours' alpha is not used.

blendWithOriginal.description: 0-1: how much of the original comes back; 0 is the full ramp.

Undo.description: Reverse the latest applied batch, or the latest one `module` issued.

UnexpressibleToken.description:
A source value the current token contract cannot express.

Keeping the original value is part of the report: a path and a vague
message are not enough for a human to judge whether accepting the draft
would discard a load-bearing brand rule.

UnlinkPath.description: Take one path out of its link (11.112): it keeps the path it has, and is independent from then on.

Unmult.description:
Unmult: turns the distance from a black or white background into coverage, and (by default)
takes the background back out of the colour.

blackLevel.description: 0-1: how bright a pixel on a black background has to be to start to show.

softness.description: 0-1: the ramp from clear to solid.

whiteLevel.description: 0-1: how far from white a pixel on a white background has to be to start to show.

UnmultBackground.description: The colour Unmult takes out of the picture.

UpdateFont.description:
Change a font's display name, fallbacks or enabled state (11.13).
Switching off a font something names is refused, as removing it is.

UpdateKeyframe.description: Replace a key that already exists at `keyframe.frame`.

VertexKind.description: How a path vertex's handles behave (11.113, pen spec v2 section 4).

oneOf.description: Handles move independently (or are absent).
Handles stay collinear and opposite; each keeps its own length.
Handles stay collinear, opposite and of equal length.
Handles are derived from the neighbours; stored ones are ignored.

Vibrance.description:
Vibrance: saturation weighted `(1 - s) * min(s, 0.5)`: a grey and a fully
saturated colour are left alone, and a half-saturated one gains most.

VideoLimiter.description:
Video Limiter: keeps every pixel inside a legal range, softly bending the highlights first;
optionally paints the pixels it had to change in a warning colour.

WritingMode.description: CSS `writing-mode` values, which is what the shaper (3.6) consumes.

description:
The one editor command type. Every authoring mutation, from every
surface (Tauri, MCP), is a value of this type.
